The current standard form is structured as 亼 above 乛. This describes its present written shape, not its ancient construction. Early oracle-bone and bronze forms are described as having a mouth-like upper part and a lower mark, sometimes omitted; the mark’s referent is disputed. One book interprets the early mark as indicating 口吟, “mouth groaning or chanting,” and proposes that temporal use displaced this meaning in Shang writing. Other accounts leave open mouth-related and wooden-clapper interpretations, so the proposed original meaning and borrowing path remain unsettled. A later Shuowen analysis divides 今 into 亼 and 乁, identifying 乁 as an ancient form of 及; this dictionary account does not settle the early graph’s construction. Separately, 今 is documented as a phonetic element in 吟, but that later role does not establish groaning or chanting as its original meaning.

The phrase 今夕其雨 attests the temporal meaning “now” or “today” in Shang oracle-bone writing. This is the earliest attested temporal use in the supplied evidence; whether another meaning preceded it remains unresolved.

A book proposes that the early graph indicated 口吟, “mouth groaning or chanting.” This is a disputed proposal about the graph’s original meaning, not an independently established use of 今; its chronology and proposed displacement by temporal use remain unresolved.
